_comment: br-frankenpandas-eay9h. ONE fixture, named explicitly, because bulk
regeneration is forbidden and this pin is load-bearing evidence.
WHAT CHANGED IN THE ORACLE. `_pivot_sort` defaulted to False -- the
historical hardcoded override -- against pandas' documented default of
True. It now defaults to True, the same way `_pivot_dropna` was settled
on 2026-08-17. Of the 15 oracle-comparing pivot_table cases, sort=True
moves exactly this ONE, because it is the only multi-value case in the
corpus (enumerated: every other fixture and every conformance_reshape /
live_oracle case passes a single-element pivot_values).
WHY THIS IS NOT LAUNDERING FP'S ANSWER INTO THE CORPUS. Until today FP
ordered multi-value output by the caller's `values` argument, which is not
a rule pandas has, and re-banking this fixture alone would have pinned
that. MEASURED, live pandas 2.2.3, one frame, both spellings:
values=[sales,profit] sort=True   profit_A profit_B sales_A sales_B
values=[profit,sales] sort=True   profit_A profit_B sales_A sales_B
values=[sales,profit] sort=False  sales_A sales_B profit_A profit_B
values=[profit,sales] sort=False  sales_A sales_B profit_A profit_B
pandas does not move when the caller reorders `values`: sort=True is
alphabetical by value name, sort=False is the FRAME's column order.
DataFrame::pivot_table_multi_values was changed in the same unit of work
to implement the sort=True rule (it exposes no sort knob, so it must
implement the default), pinned by
pivot_table_multi_values_orders_columns_by_name_not_by_argument_eay9h on a
frame where argument order, frame order and name order all DISAGREE --
which this fixture cannot do, since it lists its two values in frame order
and they are already sorted. That coincidence is why the corpus certified
FP's wrong rule twice over.
So the fixture moves to PANDAS' answer and FP moves to it independently;
neither was fitted to the other.

fp_p2d_127_dataframe_pivot_table_multi_v.evidence: live pandas 2.2.3: pd.pivot_table(df, index='region', columns='product', values=['sales','profit'], aggfunc='sum') with the fixture's own frame yields column order profit_A profit_B sales_A sales_B under pandas' sort=True default, and the SAME order when values is spelled ['profit','sales']
